en.title: Data Locations After Sequential Moves
en.description:
The initial positions are pairwise distinct. In order, move the data at position from to position to; the original guarantees that at every step from holds data and to does not. Finally, output all positions that hold data in ascending order.

This site independently prepared the standard I/O and the solution; bounds supplemented where the source lacks them and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the specification.
en.input: The first line contains n m, the second line contains n initial positions, followed by m lines of from to. The original gives no value bounds; this site adds 0≤n,m≤200000 and each position ID is in −10^9..10^9. The input satisfies the original valid-move guarantee above, so when n=0, m can only be 0.
en.output: The first line is the number of positions n, and the second line is the positions in ascending order; when n=0 the second line is empty.
en.explanation: The first example ends with 1 2 3 6. The original explanation of the second example mistakenly reused a different set of moves; this site explains it with the actual input 1→4, 4→7, 5→1, 7→3. The remaining examples end with only position 2 and with no positions, respectively.
hints: Keep the positions that hold data in a set; for each move, remove from and add to, then sort at the end.
